subject: Why the historical publication receipt reported all_match=true despite the Windows mismatch

generation_procedure.how_manifest_computed: hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest() on Linux checkout — Path.read_bytes() returns LF bytes (10231 B) on Linux because core.autocrlf default is false/input on Linux
generation_procedure.why_no_crlf_detected: Linux sandbox never exercises core.autocrlf=true CRLF conversion; generation environment is not Windows-equivalent

readback_procedure.method: GitHub Git Blobs API at the merge commit; base64-decoded bytes re-hashed locally, identity and size
readback_procedure.what_all_match_true_means: 9/9 artifacts' remote Git blob bytes (LF) are byte-identical to local Linux sandbox bytes (LF). It validates repository<->remote consistency, not repository<->Windows working-tree consistency.
readback_procedure.what_it_did_not_validate: Windows working-tree rendering with core.autocrlf=true CRLF conversion (10425 B, 7C6D44...) — because neither the manifest generation nor the read-back modeled autocrlf translation

powershell_failure.attempts: Extract exact blob bytes using PowerShell failed
powershell_failure.why: PowerShell Get-Content, string pipelines, and Out-File perform encoding/line-ending normalization (UTF-8/BOM heuristics, CRLF default). They do not return raw 10231-byte LF blob bytes without explicit -Raw -AsByteStream handling, which was not correctly used. No valid exact-byte comparison had been completed prior to this investigation.
powershell_failure.correct_method: git cat-file -p <blob> on Linux, or [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes / git show HEAD:<path> --binary on Windows with eol=lf honored

fault_attribution.hashing_procedure_deficient: omission: did not enforce eol=lf and did not test Windows CRLF rendering
